1. CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(O)=O)C=C1 - This compound is p-toluenesulfonic acid. The sulfonic acid group (SO3H) is a very strong electron-withdrawing group, making this a very acidic compound.

2. CCN(CC)CC - This compound is triethylamine, which is a basic compound due to the presence of the basic amine group. It is not acidic.

3. SC1=CC=C([N+]([O-])=O)C=C1 - This compound is p-nitrothiophene. The nitro group is an electron-withdrawing group, which can increase acidity compared to compounds without such groups, but it is not as acidic as sulfonic acids.

From this analysis, the order of acidity from most acidic to least acidic would be:
- p-toluenesulfonic acid (CC1=CC=C(S(=O)(O)=O)C=C1)
- p-nitrothiophene (SC1=CC=C([N+]([O-])=O)C=C1)
- triethylamine (CCN(CC)CC)
